results.content:
“Hyundai Motor Group remains committed to the long-term growth of the U.S. automotive industry through localized production and innovation,” Bianca Johnson, a Hyundai spokesperson, wrote in an email to _State Affairs_. “With nearly four decades of investment in America, including a new $21 billion commitment, Hyundai Motor Group is expanding U.S. production to 1.2 million vehicles across Alabama, Georgia and our new Metaplant in Savannah, making the majority of our U.S. sales locally built.” [...] Representatives from Hyundai, which recently opened a $7.6 billion electric vehicle factory outside Savannah and has pledged $21 billion in local investment, declined to comment about their forecasts for the tariffs — other than to say that prices for Hyundai cars will not change before June 2. [...] The 25% auto tariff could pose a major threat to automobile titans like Hyundai and Kia that have production plants in the state, said Jennifer Safavian, president and CEO of the trade group Autos Drive America.

Safavian said her group recently conducted a study that indicates a 25% tariff on top of the 10% global levy would prompt a “sharp decline” in U.S. auto production and an average $4,000 increase in the price of new vehicles.
